gloss: public stage; the spotlight; center stage

definitions.gloss: public stage; the spotlight; front stage of public life
definitions.explanation: The visible, public arena where important events take place or where a person is in the public eye. Often used figuratively for someone's public career or prominence.

examples.japanese: {表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{立|た}つ。
examples.english: To stand on the public stage.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{裏方|うらかた}だった{彼|かれ}が、ついに{表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: After years behind the scenes, he finally stepped into the spotlight.

examples.japanese: {引退|いんたい}した{政治家|せいじか}が{再|ふたた}び{表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{戻|もど}ってくるとは{誰|だれ}も{予想|よそう}しなかった。
examples.english: No one expected the retired politician to return to the public stage.

notes:
Composed of {表|おもて} (front, surface, public) + {舞台|ぶたい} (stage). The metaphor of a stage is central — the {表舞台|おもてぶたい} is where things are visible to the public, in contrast to the behind-the-scenes world.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{立|た}つ (stand on the public stage)
- {表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{出|で}る (step into the spotlight)
- {表舞台|おもてぶたい}から{姿|すがた}を{消|け}す (disappear from the public eye)
- {表舞台|おもてぶたい}に{戻|もど}る (return to the spotlight)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {裏方|うらかた} — behind the scenes (the opposite: those who work out of public view)
- {舞台|ぶたい} — stage (literal or figurative, without the specific "public" nuance)
- {檜舞台|ひのきぶたい} — grand stage (the most prestigious stage, implies a big moment)
